caveats.summary: eCFR lists only agencies that have a chapter in the Code of Federal Regulations. For a non-regulatory or non-executive body, having no CFR chapter is correct rather than opaque, and is recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE rather than ABSENT.

The Federal Register agency list covers bodies that submit documents for publication in the Federal Register. It retains defunct agencies as first-class entries and carries no active/abolished flag, so the absence of an agency is ambiguous and its presence does not imply it still exists.

PLUM omits at least 7 federal entities and at least 130 Senate-confirmed positions, and contains inconsistent identifiers and duplicate positions. OPM concurred with all recommendations. Absence from PLUM is therefore evidence of a gap in PLUM, not proof that an agency has no such positions.

description.value: The Selective Service System provides manpower to the Armed Forces in an emergency and operates an Alternative Service Program during a draft for men classified as conscientious objectors. The Selective Service System was established by the Military Selective Service Act (50 U.S.C. app. 451-471a). The act requires the registration of male citizens of the United States and all other male persons who are in the United States and who are ages 18 to 25. The act exempts members of the active Armed Forces and nonimmigrant aliens. Proclamation 4771 of July 20, 1980, requires male persons born on or after January 1, 1960, and who have attained age 18 but have not attained age 26 to register. The act imposes liability for training and service in the Armed Forces upon registrants who are ages 18 to 26, except those who are exempt or deferred. Persons who have been deferred remain liable for training and service until age 35. Aliens are not liable for training and service until they have remained in the United States for more than 1 year. Conscientious objectors who are found to be opposed to all service in the Armed Forces are required to perform civilian work in lieu of induction into the Armed Forces.The authority to induct registrants, including doctors and allied medical specialists, expired July 1, 1973.
